mcqs.question: What is the definition of the principal focus of a lens?

options.A: The point on the principal axis where parallel rays after refraction converge (for a convex lens) or appear to diverge (for a concave lens).
options.B: The point at which the lens is thickest.
options.C: The centre of curvature of the lens surface.
options.D: The point where an image is formed when the object is placed at infinity.

mcqs.answer: The point on the principal axis where parallel rays after refraction converge (for a convex lens) or appear to diverge (for a concave lens).
mcqs.explanation: The principal focus (F) is defined as the point on the principal axis where rays that were initially parallel to that axis either meet (convex lens) or seem to originate (concave lens) after passing through the lens. Options B, C and D describe unrelated features.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image on a screen 30 cm from the lens when the object is placed 60 cm from the lens. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (taking u = –60 cm, v = +30 cm), we get 1/f = 1/30 – 1/60 = 1/60, so f = 60 cm. Hence option D is correct; the other values do not satisfy the formula.

mcqs.question: Which of the following rays is NOT used in the standard ray diagram for a convex lens?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis that refracts through the focal point on the other side.
options.B: A ray passing through the optical centre of the lens and continuing undeviated.
options.C: A ray directed towards the focal point on the object side that emerges parallel to the principal axis.
options.D: A ray that reflects off the surface of the lens.

mcqs.answer: A ray that reflects off the surface of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: Standard ray diagrams for refraction use three rays: parallel‑then‑through‑focus, through‑focus‑then‑parallel, and through‑optical‑centre (undeviated). Reflection does not occur in thin‑lens refraction, making option D incorrect. Options A‑C are the three conventional rays.

mcqs.question: An object is placed at a distance of 2f from a convex lens of focal length f. Which statement correctly describes the image formed?

options.A: A real, inverted image of the same size formed at 2f on the opposite side of the lens.
options.B: A real, upright image that is magnified and formed at the focal point.
options.C: A virtual, upright image of the same size formed at 2f on the same side as the object.
options.D: A virtual, inverted image that is reduced and formed at the focal point.

mcqs.answer: A real, inverted image of the same size formed at 2f on the opposite side of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, when the object is at 2f, the image is formed at 2f on the other side, is real, inverted, and of the same size. Options B, C, and D describe situations that occur for other object positions.

mcqs.question: Identify the incorrect statement about convex and concave lenses.

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus.
options.B: A concave lens diverges parallel rays so that they appear to come from a virtual focus.
options.C: A concave lens can produce a real, inverted image of a distant object.
options.D: A convex lens is thicker at the centre than at the edges.

mcqs.answer: A concave lens can produce a real, inverted image of a distant object.
mcqs.explanation: Concave lenses always produce virtual, upright, and reduced images; they never form real, inverted images. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the respective lenses.

mcqs.question: Why is the optical centre of a thin lens considered the point through which a ray passes undeviated?

options.A: Because the lens thickness is zero at that point.
options.B: Because the two surfaces of the lens are locally parallel at the centre, giving equal angles of incidence and refraction.
options.C: Because the refractive index of the material is lower at the centre.
options.D: Because the principal axis bends at that point.

mcqs.answer: Because the two surfaces of the lens are locally parallel at the centre, giving equal angles of incidence and refraction.
mcqs.explanation: At the optical centre the incident ray meets two nearly parallel surfaces, so the angle of incidence equals the angle of refraction on both sides, resulting in no net deviation. Options A, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: How does the location of the principal focus differ between a convex lens and a concave lens?

options.A: In a convex lens it lies on the same side as the incoming light; in a concave lens it lies on the opposite side.
options.B: In a convex lens it lies on the opposite side of the incoming light; in a concave lens it lies on the same side as the incoming light.
options.C: Both lenses have the principal focus on the same side as the incoming light.
options.D: Neither lens has a principal focus.

mcqs.answer: In a convex lens it lies on the opposite side of the incoming light; in a concave lens it lies on the same side as the incoming light.
mcqs.explanation: For a converging (convex) lens, parallel rays meet at the focus on the side opposite the incident light. For a diverging (concave) lens, the rays appear to diverge from a virtual focus on the same side as the incident light. Options A, C, and D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms an image of a candle placed 20 cm from the lens at a distance of 30 cm on the other side. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (taking u = –20 cm, v = +30 cm), we get 1/f = 1/30 – 1/20 = (2‑3)/60 = –1/60. The magnitude gives f = 60/5 = 12 cm (sign indicates a converging lens). Hence option B is correct; the other values do not satisfy the formula.
